# Test data provenance

Everything under `testdata/spp/` is vendored from the reference implementation this project
is validated against. Nothing here was written by hand; using real mission files is the
whole point — a hand-rolled XTCE fixture would only test the assumptions of whoever wrote it.

## Upstream

| | |
|---|---|
| Project | [`lasp/space_packet_parser`](https://github.com/lasp/space_packet_parser) |
| Commit | `6de220ff25e75d0a8b6258086f9d99ce9eae820b` (2026-08-07) |
| Version | 6.1.2 |
| Path | `tests/test_data/` |
| Licence | BSD 3-Clause, © 2023 University of Colorado — see `testdata/spp/LICENSE.txt` |

The BSD 3-Clause licence permits redistribution provided the copyright notice and licence
text are retained, which `testdata/spp/LICENSE.txt` does.

## Files

### Definition + packet-stream pairs (used by the differential tests)

| Definition | Packet stream | Packets | Exercises |

| `jpss/jpss1_geolocation_xtce_v1.xml` | `jpss/J01_G011_LZ_2021-04-09T00-00-00Z_V01.DAT1` | 7200 | container inheritance, `ComparisonList`, IEEE-754 floats |
| `jpss/contrived_inheritance_structure.xml` | (same stream) | 7200 | `BooleanExpression`, `ANDedConditions`, `Condition` |
| `ctim/ctim_xtce_v1.xml` | `ctim/ccsds_2021_155_14_39_51` | 1499 | 1.6 MB definition, `twosComplement`, fixed-size UTF-8 strings |
| `suda/suda_combined_science_definition.xml` | `suda/sciData_2022_130_17_41_53.spl` | 13 | enumerations, dynamically sized binary (`DynamicValue` + `LinearAdjustment`); stream needs `skip_header_bytes=4` |
| `idex/idex_combined_science_definition.xml` | `idex/sciData_2023_052_14_45_05` | 78 | polymorphic containers, dynamically sized binary |
| `jpss/jpss1_geolocation_xtce_v1.xml` | `ctim/ccsds_2021_155_14_39_51` | 1499 | **rejection case**: a definition pointed at a stream it does not describe, so both implementations must refuse every packet. Without it, the "we agree this cannot be decoded" half of the contract goes untested — the other five cases have no unrecognised packets at all |

### Written for this project

Seven files here are not vendored. All exist for the same reason: an implementation path that
the real mission files never reach, and so would never be compared against anything.

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `numeric_edges.xml` | the mission files contain one 32-bit float, no 16-bit float, and no numeric field spanning nine bytes |
| `calibrators.xml` | **no mission file has a calibrator at all** — grepping all five returns nothing |
| `boolean_criteria.xml` | the one mission file with a `<BooleanExpression>` has a single conjunction of equalities: no disjunction, no nesting, and no operator but `==` |
| `byte_order.xml` + `byte_order_stream.bin` | **no mission file sets `byteOrder`** — so there is no recorded telemetry with a little-endian field, and no bytes to put in front of the reference |
| `arrays.xml` | **no mission file has an `<ArrayParameterType>`**, and neither does the reference: it raises `NotImplementedError` and calls the feature roadmap |
| `aggregates.xml` | the same for `<AggregateParameterType>`, plus the two nested in each other, which is where the naming can go wrong |
| `mil_1750a.xml` + `mil_1750a_stream.bin` | **no mission file uses MIL-STD-1750A** — but the reference implements it, so this one is a golden case like the six real ones |

`byte_order_stream.bin` and `mil_1750a_stream.bin` are the only packet streams here that were
not flown. It is written by
`tools/gen_byte_order_stream.py` from a fixed seed, so regenerating it produces the same file
and the golden taken over it stays meaningful. Both are golden cases like the six real ones, which makes little-endian and MIL-STD-1750A the
only two features whose interpreted paths are checked against `space_packet_parser` directly.
Little-endian found two divergences the first time it ran; MIL-STD-1750A matched. See
`SUPPORTED.md`.

Neither is a substitute for a real sample; they are a supplement to one. `calibrators.xml` in
particular is built around a difference that only shows up in the last bit: the reference
raises an integral raw value to its power exactly and rounds once, and a float raw by
repeated squaring, which rounds at every step. Two of its parameters carry identical
polynomial terms over the two encodings so that a generator collapsing them into one routine
is caught.

## Golden files

`testdata/golden/*.json` are generated by `tools/gen_goldens.py` running the Python
reference, and are committed so that CI needs no Python interpreter. Each file holds:

* full raw and engineering values for the first 64 packets;
* a SHA-256 digest over the canonical encoding of **every** packet in the stream, so a
  mismatch in the tail cannot hide behind the truncated detail section;
* the reference implementation's own load and parse timings, as the baseline for `xtce bench`.

Regenerate with:

```console
$ python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install space_packet_parser==6.1.2
$ .venv/bin/python tools/gen_goldens.py
```

Values are encoded losslessly: integers as JSON numbers, floats as `{"f": "<float.hex()>"}`
so the IEEE-754 bit pattern round-trips exactly, and bytes as `{"b": "<hex>"}`.
